head.meta_description: How to choose a caterer in Dubai: what a licensed caterer should show you, how to compare quotes on the same brief, and the questions that matter.
head.h1: How to Choose a Caterer in Dubai — Real Prices and Timings

opening_paragraph: A good caterer in Dubai is licensed, names the chef and quotes every line. Knowing how to choose caterer Dubai comes down to four things myCHEF puts in writing: transparent pricing from around AED 1,200, confirmed dietary fit, vetted chefs, and an itemised proposal before you book. Here is the process, explained without the sales gloss, with the practical tips you need to compare any Dubai caterer and stop guessing.
leave_untouched: What to Check Before You Book

add_block.new_heading: Why does transparent pricing matter most?
new_paragraphs: Because a clear price is the fastest trust signal you get. The surest sign of a reliable Dubai caterer is a visible price, not a blanket "request a quote". Look for per-person ranges or packages up front, then an itemised proposal for your date. As a rough guide, an intimate catered dinner at home in Dubai often starts from around AED 1,200, a mid-size private party lands nearer AED 2,400, and a larger villa event can run to AED 4,500 or beyond once staffing, styling and equipment are added. Comparing the cost of two caterers only works when both list what the number covers. If one quote looks far cheaper, check whether it includes service staff, setup and cleanup, or is only drop-off food. Our own prices guide breaks these ranges down so you can benchmark any quote you receive.

add_block.new_heading: How do I confirm cuisine and dietary fit?
new_paragraphs: Ask directly, and expect specifics, not a token "we can do that". Dubai events are gloriously multicultural, so a caterer should handle your full cuisine mix and every dietary need: halal, vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, nut-free and real allergy management. Share restrictions early and a good team prepares separate dishes and labels each one. At myCHEF, chefs such as Layla Hassan build Arabic and halal menus that sit comfortably beside, say, an Italian or Mediterranean spread, so a mixed guest list is not an afterthought. Ask to see a sample menu for your kind of event, and confirm how allergens are kept apart in the kitchen. The UAE treats this seriously: under federal food-safety rules, misleading food descriptions can draw fines, so precise labelling is both good hospitality and the law. If a caterer waves away dietary questions, read it as a warning sign.

add_block.new_heading: How are the chefs vetted, and is the food safe?
new_paragraphs: Start with two questions: who is coming into my home, and is the kitchen compliant? UAE food safety is governed by Federal Law No. 10 of 2015, and in Dubai the Food Safety Department of Dubai Municipality licenses food businesses and inspects restaurants and catering operations, as the UAE government portal confirms . On the people side, ask how chefs are checked. MyCHEF runs identity checks, a practical cooking assessment, reference verification and ongoing reviews before and after a chef such as Ahmed Al-Rashid joins the network. You can read the full method on how we vet chefs . A caterer who can explain both their food-safety compliance and their hiring checks has nothing to hide. One that cannot is a gamble with your guests' evening.

add_block.new_heading: How to choose caterer Dubai: the questions to ask
new_paragraphs: The short version of how to choose caterer Dubai is a checklist you can run in a single phone call. Ask exactly what is included: chefs, service staff, tableware, setup and cleanup. Ask the deposit and cancellation terms, and get them in writing. Ask how far ahead to book and whether your date falls in peak season.Finally, ask for an itemised proposal, not a lump sum. Clear answers to this catering company checklist separate a smooth event from a stressful one. The reliable way to find reputable caterers is to run the same questions past three of them and watch which one answers without hedging. The common red flags are easy to spot once you are listening for them: catering companies that will not put a price in writing, that quote a lump sum with no breakdown, that stay vague about who is actually cooking, or that press for a large deposit before you have seen a menu. Keep the replies side by side. The right caterer is usually the one who answers plainly and fastest, not the one with the glossiest brochure or the most confident sales patter.

add_block.new_heading: What should a good catering proposal include?
new_paragraphs: A proper proposal reads like a plan, not a price tag. Expect the full menu with courses and quantities, the number of chefs and service staff, arrival and service timings, equipment and styling, and a single itemised total with the deposit shown. Catering services in Dubai usually cover menu planning, cooking, setup, serving and cleanup, so confirm each line is there and not just assumed. If styling, waiters or a mocktail bar are extra, they should be named, not buried in a round number. A vague one-line quote makes it hard to compare two caterers side by side, which is exactly why itemised proposals matter. When you brief a caterer, give the date, guest count, venue and any dietary needs up front. The more precise your brief, the more accurate the proposal, and the fewer surprises on the night itself.

add_block.new_heading: How far ahead should I book?
new_paragraphs: Book as early as you reasonably can, especially for busy 2026 dates. Weekends, Ramadan, UAE National Day and the cooler December-to-March season fill quickly, and the best chefs get reserved first. For a standard private dinner, a few weeks of planning is often enough; for a wedding or a large villa event, think a couple of months. Off-peak weekday events are usually easier to staff and can be gentler on cost. If you are searching for a private caterer near me at the last minute, be honest about your timeline so the team can tell you what is deliverable instead of overpromising. Good planning also means confirming venue access, kitchen space and power early. Once your brief is clear, myCHEF can usually turn an itemised proposal around within one business day.

add_block.new_heading: What are the best ideas for matching a caterer to your event?
new_paragraphs: Match the caterer to the occasion, not the other way round. A relaxed villa barbecue, a plated anniversary dinner and a corporate launch each reward different strengths, so the best ideas start with the mood you want to create. For an intimate meal, a private chef cooking in your kitchen often beats a large catering brigade; for a hundred guests, a full catering team with service staff makes more sense. Think about flow: canapes and a mocktail bar for a mingling crowd, or a set menu for a seated celebration. Ask the caterer which format they would recommend for your guest count and venue, then judge whether the reasoning sounds experienced or scripted. The right partner offers a considered opinion, adapts to your space, and treats your event as theirs to get right.

new_paragraphs: What is the short answer to choosing a caterer in Dubai?

Look for transparent pricing, confirm they cover your cuisine and dietary needs, check that chefs are vetted and food-safety aware, ask exactly what is included, and get an itemised proposal before you book.
How much does catering in Dubai cost?

An intimate catered dinner at home often starts from around AED 1,200, a mid-size private party lands nearer AED 2,400, and a larger villa event can run to AED 4,500 or more once staff, styling and equipment are added. Your final price depends on the menu and guest count.
How do I get an exact quote?
Share your date, guest count and venue with myCHEF and you will get an itemised proposal, usually within one business day.
Do Dubai caterers handle halal and dietary needs?

A good caterer handles halal, vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, nut-free and allergy needs, prepares separate dishes and labels each one. Share your restrictions early so the menu is planned around them.
How far ahead should I book a caterer?
Book as early as you can. A private dinner may need only a few weeks, while a wedding or large villa event is better booked a couple of months ahead, especially for peak 2026 dates.
What questions should be on my caterer checklist?
Ask what is included, the deposit and cancellation terms, how far ahead to book, for references or case studies, and for an itemised proposal rather than a lump sum.
Are caterers in Dubai regulated?
Yes. UAE food safety is governed by Federal Law No. 10 of 2015, and Dubai Municipality licenses food businesses and inspects restaurants and catering operations across the emirate.
